standard.title: Partition three-digit numbers
standard.description: partition, rearrange, regroup and rename two- and three-digit numbers using standard and non-standard groupings; recognise the role of a zero digit in place value notation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students partition one- and two-digit numbers in different ways including into tens and ones (AC9M1N02). They have not yet partitioned three-digit numbers, worked with non-standard groupings, or reasoned about zero as a placeholder.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students partition, rearrange, regroup and rename two- and three-digit numbers using standard and non-standard groupings, and explain the role of zero as a placeholder in place value notation.

nodes.label: Standard partitioning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can partition a three-digit number into hundreds, tens and ones using materials and explain the value of each part.
nodes.minimum_width: Partition at least two three-digit numbers into hundreds, tens and ones using base-ten materials; match to expanded form (e.g. 300 + 40 + 5).
nodes.typical_width: Partition a range of three-digit numbers including those with a zero digit; represent as expanded notation; compare the digits of a numeral with grouped materials.
wider: Partition three-digit numbers with zero in different positions (tens, ones, hundreds) and explain why the numeral still has three digits
Use a range of materials (base-ten blocks, bundling sticks, collections of objects) to represent the same number and compare the representations
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 non-standard regrouping requires students to reason about how many tens are contained in a hundreds group. Students who omit zeros or misread place value cannot perform this reasoning — they cannot regroup what they have not correctly partitioned.

response_modes.reason: Zero as a placeholder is a persistent misconception — students may omit zeros or misread 305 as 35. Multiple representations across different contexts (materials, expanded form, numerals) help consolidate the concept that zero holds a position even when no quantity occupies it.

success_criteria: Partitions a three-digit number into hundreds, tens and ones using materials
Writes the expanded form of a three-digit number including one with a zero digit

nodes.label: Non-standard regrouping
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can rename a three-digit number using non-standard groupings (e.g. 245 as 24 tens and 5 ones) and explain why both representations are equivalent.
nodes.minimum_width: Rename one three-digit number in at least one non-standard way using materials; explain why the value is unchanged.
nodes.typical_width: Rename two- and three-digit numbers in multiple ways using standard and non-standard groupings; use knowledge of place value to explain equivalence; e.g. 245 as 2 hundreds 45 ones or 24 tens 5 ones.
wider: Find all possible ways to rename a given three-digit number using different groupings; record systematically and look for patterns
Use non-standard partitioning to assist mental addition: e.g. rename 138 as 13 tens and 8 ones to add 40 more

response_modes.reason: Non-standard regrouping requires students to reason through equivalence explicitly — it is not immediately obvious that 24 tens and 5 ones equals 245. The reasoning scaffold of 'how many tens are in 2 hundreds?' needs to be made visible before students can apply it independently.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Finding all possible renamings and recording them systematically offers genuine richness — students begin to see multiplicative relationships between place value units (10 ones = 1 ten, 10 tens = 1 hundred) as a generalisable structure, not just a fact about one number.
success_criteria: Renames a three-digit number in at least one non-standard way using materials
Explains why the renamed form represents the same quantity as the standard form
